title: Who Am I? Profiles, Identity, and Regions
intro: The most dangerous AWS command is the right command run in the wrong account. Before touching anything, a professional checks which identity, account, and region the CLI will act as. At a company with dozens of accounts (dev, staging, prod, security, billing), this habit prevents real disasters.

steps.prompt: List the named profiles configured on this machine.
steps.explanation: Five profiles, one per account and role you can use.
steps.why: Named profiles (in ~/.aws/config) keep each account's credentials separate. That beats one 'default' profile you keep overwriting with 'aws configure', which is how people end up running a dev script against prod.

steps.prompt: Ask AWS who you actually are right now with the default profile.
steps.explanation: You're alice, using an assumed role (DeveloperAccess) in account 111122223333.
steps.why: get-caller-identity needs no permissions and always works, so it's the universal 'where am I?' check. The ARN also tells you whether you're a long-lived IAM user (arn:...:user/) or a temporary assumed role (arn:...:assumed-role/), which matters for security reviews.

steps.prompt: Check the identity behind the prod-readonly profile before using it.
steps.explanation: prod-readonly is a read-only role in the production account 444455556666.
steps.why: --profile applies to a single command. Starting an investigation with a read-only role means a typo can't delete anything; switch to the admin profile only for the one command that needs it.

steps.prompt: Make prod-readonly the profile for the rest of this shell session, using an environment variable.
steps.fake_output: (no output: every aws command in this shell now uses prod-readonly)
steps.why: Environment variables override the default profile but only live as long as this shell, which is safer than changing the default. Tools like direnv or aws-vault set this per project directory automatically. Show the profile in your shell prompt so you always see it.

steps.prompt: List the regions enabled for this account, as plain text.
steps.fake_output: us-east-1	us-east-2	us-west-2	eu-west-1	eu-central-1	ap-southeast-1
steps.why: Most AWS resources are regional: an instance in eu-west-1 doesn't appear in a us-east-1 listing at all. 'It's gone!' is very often 'you're looking at the wrong region'. --query (JMESPath) and --output text turn verbose JSON into exactly the field you need, which is the key skill for scripting the CLI.
